title: Shoyu Ramen
kicker: Clear chicken-soy broth, jammy eggs, springy noodles — the Tokyo classic, built from scratch.
story: Shoyu ramen is the original ramen — the Tokyo standard, soy-sauce seasoned, clear rather than milky, built on a broth of chicken (often with vegetables) that tastes clean and deeply savory rather than heavy. Where tonkotsu shouts, shoyu speaks at a normal volume and somehow holds the whole room.

The bowl is assembled in layers, and that is the real lesson of making ramen at home: broth, tare (the seasoning base), aroma oil, noodles, toppings — each one seasoned on its own merit. A soft egg marinated overnight. Chashu pork braised and torched. Scallions cut fine. None of it is hard; all of it adds up to something much larger than a noodle soup has any right to be.
fun_fact: Ramen arrived in Japan via Chinese immigrants in the late 1800s. 'Shoyu' just means soy sauce — the tare style, not the noodle. Tokyo's oldest surviving ramen shop, Rairaiken, opened in 1910.

ingredients.item: chicken backs/wings or a whole carcass
ingredients.note: for a clear broth, no rolling boil
fresh from an Asian grocer changes everything

steps.title: Char the aromatics
steps.text: Broil onion, scallion, ginger and garlic until blackened at the edges. Charred, not burned — this builds the broth's backbone without clouding it.

steps.title: A clear broth is a gentle broth
steps.text: Cover chicken and aromatics with 3 L cold water. Bring to a bare simmer — bubbles occasionally breaking the surface, never a boil — and cook 3 hours, skimming. Boiling emulsifies fat into milky cloudiness; you want clarity.

steps.title: Make the tare
steps.text: Combine soy sauce, mirin and 120 ml of the finished broth in a small saucepan; warm through. This concentrated seasoning goes into the bowl first — never season the whole pot.

steps.title: Eggs and pork
steps.text: Boil eggs exactly 6.5 minutes from fridge-cold, ice bath, peel, marinate overnight in equal soy and mirin thinned with a splash of water. Slice chashu thin; torch or sear the edges until they smell like a festival.

steps.title: Noodles last, always
steps.text: Cook fresh noodles in unsalted boiling water 60-90 seconds — fresh ramen cooks in the time it takes to breathe. Drain well. Meanwhile heat the bowls with hot water.

steps.title: Assemble like you mean it
steps.text: Per bowl: 40 ml tare, 400 ml hot broth, a teaspoon of sesame oil. Add noodles, lift them once with chopsticks to fold. Top with pork, egg halves, scallions, nori. Eat immediately, loudly, with unembarrassed slurping.

notes: Broth and tare keep 4-5 days refrigerated; the broth also freezes. Ramen is genuinely better on day two.
No fresh noodles? Dried work — but cook them a minute less than the package says.
For a lighter weeknight version, good store-bought chicken stock + tare + fresh toppings gets you 80% of the way in 20 minutes.
